column1: In CSS/DOM animation work, why should decorative particles often use `position: absolute`?
column2: So they’re removed from normal layout flow and don’t affect the size or position of surrounding elements.

column1: In a particle effect, how can you quickly place particles in varied locations within a container?
column2: Assign randomized positional values, such as `top` and `left` percentages, to each particle.

column1: Why can an element animated from `opacity: 1` to `opacity: 0` appear visible again after the animation ends?
column2: Because keyframe styles apply only while the animation is running unless a fill mode or base style preserves the final state.

column1: In CSS animations, what does `animation-fill-mode: forwards` do?
column2: It keeps the element in the final keyframe state after the animation finishes.

column1: When building a complex animation effect, why is it useful to start with a minimal version first?
column2: It reduces complexity, makes debugging easier, and lets you validate one part of the effect before layering on more behavior.
